# Sentido de Pertenencia: Lasting Special Places

## Special habitats mentioned by the EWG 

### Coquina reefs 

```{r}
coquina_reefs_tnc <- st_read(here::here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/_raw_data/TNC_geoportal_fishing_refuge_zones/d2026/Arrecifes_de_coquina_-7828932449339036258.geojson"))

ohi_rgns <- st_read(here("spatial/ohi_regions/goc_ohi_rgns.shp")) 

# intersect with GoC rgns
coquina_reefs_tnc_rgnid <- st_intersection(st_transform(coquina_reefs_tnc, st_crs(ohi_rgns)), ohi_rgns)
mapview(coquina_reefs_tnc_rgnid, zcol = "rgn_id")

coquina_reef_lsps <- coquina_reefs_tnc_rgnid %>% 
  mutate(lsp_name = paste0(FID, id, sep = ": ", "Coquina Reefs in Libertad, Bahia Lobos, and Peñasco - AHW")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(rgn_id, lsp_name)
mapview(coquina_reef_lsps, zcol = "lsp_name")

write_csv(coquina_reef_lsps, here::here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/goal_prep/sp/lsp/v2025/int/coquina_reef_lsps.csv"))
```

## Determine if they overlap with protected areas

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(sf)
library(mapview)
library(stringdist)
library(stringi)
```


```{r}
# ============================================================
# 0. Load shared spatial layers (used across all habitats)
# ============================================================

ohi_rgns <- st_read(here("spatial/ohi_regions/goc_ohi_rgns.shp"))

inland_10 <- st_read(here::here(
  "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/inland_10km_buffer",
  "inland_10km_goc.shp"
))

regions_marine <- ohi_rgns %>% filter(location == "marine")

marine_and_inland10 <- bind_rows(regions_marine, inland_10) %>%
  dplyr::select(rgn_id, geometry) %>%
  group_by(rgn_id) %>%
  summarize(geometry = st_union(geometry))

# Protected areas (combined WDPA + HEM layer, created in dive sites script)
all_protected <- st_read(here::here(
  "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/protected _areas_wdpa_and_hem",
  "all_goc_protected_areas_2025.shp"
))

all_protected_dissolved <- st_read(here::here(
  "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/protected _areas_wdpa_and_hem",
  "all_goc_protected_areas_dissolved_2025.shp"
))

# SIMEC i-efectividad
i_efectividad_raw <- read_csv(here::here(
  "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/_raw_data/SIMEC/identifying_lasting_special_places_SIMEC.csv"
)) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

# Ramsar management plans (present/absent)
ramsar_management_plans <- read_csv(here::here(
  "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/goal_prep/sp/lsp/v2025/ramsar_site_management_plans.csv"
))
```


```{r}
# NOM baseline condition for each special habitat
NOM_MANGROVE_CONDITION <- 70

# Ley General de Vida Silvestre Art. 60ter (prohibition of cutting/filling mangroves); Código Penal Art. 420bis (potential for prison); NOM-022-SEMARNAT-2003; NOM-059; LGEEPA	80	strong	"""Article 60 TER.- The removal, filling, transplanting, pruning, or any work or activity that affects the integrity of the hydrological flow of the mangrove is prohibited."" https://www.diputados.gob.mx/LeyesBiblio/pdf/LGVS.pdf 
# ""A prison sentence of two to ten years and a fine equivalent to three hundred to three thousand days' wages will be imposed on anyone who unlawfully....Damage, dry up or fill wetlands, mangroves, lagoons, estuaries or swamps; Damage reefs; Introduce or release into the natural environment any specimen of exotic flora or fauna that harms an ecosystem, or that hinders, alters or affects native or migratory species in the natural cycles of their reproduction or migration, or; Cause a fire in a forest, jungle, natural vegetation or forest lands, which damages natural elements, flora, fauna, ecosystems or the environment. An additional penalty of up to two years in prison and up to one thousand additional days of fines will be applied when the conduct described in this article is carried out in or affects a protected natural area, or the perpetrator or accomplice of the crime provided for in section IV, carries out the conduct to obtain a profit or economic benefit. https://mexico.justia.com/federales/codigos/codigo-penal-federal/libro-segundo/titulo-vigesimoquinto/capitulo-segundo/#articulo-420-bis 
# https://www.dof.gob.mx/nota_detalle.php?codigo=697013&fecha=10/04/2003#gsc.tab=0
# https://bmasf.mx/en/environmental-impact-assessment-in-mexico/"

NOM_SEAGRASS_CONDITION <- 70
# NOM-022 coastal wetlands standard; NOM-059 (Zostera marina: Special Protection (Pr)); LGEEPA; General Wildlife Law; Ramsar Convention	80	strong

NOM_CORAL_CONDITION <- 70
# Strict vessel liability on reefs under LGEEPA and the Federal Law for Environmental Liability (LFRA); General Wildlife Law; CITES Appendix II coral spp.; may be under NOM-059 but none of the coral species that have occurred in the GoC are listed currently.	80	strong	"Environmental Impact Assessment in Mexico - Bustamante + Freyre
# A prison sentence of two to ten years and a fine equivalent to three hundred to three thousand days' wages will be imposed on anyone who unlawfully....Damage, dry up or fill wetlands, mangroves, lagoons, estuaries or swamps; Damage reefs; Introduce or release into the natural environment any specimen of exotic flora or fauna that harms an ecosystem, or that hinders, alters or affects native or migratory species in the natural cycles of their reproduction or migration, or; Cause a fire in a forest, jungle, natural vegetation or forest lands, which damages natural elements, flora, fauna, ecosystems or the environment. An additional penalty of up to two years in prison and up to one thousand additional days of fines will be applied when the conduct described in this article is carried out in or affects a protected natural area, or the perpetrator or accomplice of the crime provided for in section IV, carries out the conduct to obtain a profit or economic benefit. 
# https://mexico.justia.com/federales/codigos/codigo-penal-federal/libro-segundo/titulo-vigesimoquinto/capitulo-segundo/#articulo-420-bis
# https://axaxl.com/fast-fast-forward/articles/mexicos-new-environmental-law 
# ""Strict liability holds companies responsible for accidents that occur, despite the best oversight and maintenance. If a perfectly maintained ship is operating on a coral reef, and the ship accidentally leaks hazardous waste and damages the reef, it isn’t the result of error or negligence. The ship still caused damage to the reef, and the ship company will be held responsible. Under strict liability, the plaintiff does not have to prove that damages were the result of negligence. He only has to prove that the damages occurred, and that the defendant was somehow responsible.  """

NOM_COQUINA_CONDITION <- 30
# No dedicated habitat statute; possible indirect LGEEPA coverage if NOM-059 species present; general environmental impact rules apply	30	weak
```


## Determine if they overlap with protected areas

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 1. Helper functions
# ============================================================

normalize_name <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") %>%
    str_to_upper() %>%
    str_remove_all("\\bPARQUE NACIONAL\\b|\\bPARQUE\\b|\\bNACIONAL\\b|\\bZONA MARINA\\b|\\bARCHIPIELAGO\\b") %>%
    str_squish()
}

#' Given an sf polygon/multipolygon layer already clipped to GoC regions, this function:
#'   1. Buffers by 100m and spatial-joins to all_protected
#'   2. Fuzzy-matches protected area names to SIMEC i-efectividad
#'   3. Returns one row per habitat feature with overall_condition
#'
#' @param habitat_sf     sf object already intersected with GoC regions (has rgn_id)
#' @param name_col       bare column name to group by as the feature identifier
#' @param habitat_label  string label for the habitat type (used in messages)
#' @param nom_condition  numeric baseline condition (0-100) when outside protected areas

assign_habitat_condition <- function(habitat_sf, name_col, habitat_label, nom_condition) {

  message("--- Processing: ", habitat_label, " ---")
  message("  Input features: ", nrow(habitat_sf))

  # 1. Buffer by 100m to catch overlaps with protected area boundaries
  habitat_buffered <- st_buffer(
    st_transform(habitat_sf, st_crs(all_protected)),
    dist = 100
  )

  # 2. Spatial join to protected areas (left join — keep all features)
  habitat_protected <- st_join(
    habitat_buffered,
    all_protected %>% dplyr::select(name, geometry),
    join = st_intersects,
    left = TRUE
  ) %>%
    mutate(in_protected_area = !is.na(name)) %>%
    rename(protected_area_name = name)

  message("  In protected area: ", sum(habitat_protected$in_protected_area, na.rm = TRUE),
          " / ", nrow(habitat_protected))

  # 3. Fuzzy-match protected area names → SIMEC i-efectividad
  habitat_norm <- habitat_protected %>%
    mutate(protected_area_norm = normalize_name(protected_area_name))

  matches <- stringdist::amatch(
    habitat_norm$protected_area_norm,
    i_efectividad_norm$nombre_norm,
    method = "jw",
    maxDist = 0.2
  )

  habitat_matched <- habitat_norm %>%
    mutate(
      nombre_matched      = i_efectividad_norm$nombre[matches],
      nombre_norm_matched = i_efectividad_norm$nombre_norm[matches]
    )

  # Inspect matches before joining
 habitat_matched %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    distinct(protected_area_name, protected_area_norm, nombre_matched) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    print(n = Inf)
 
 # 4. Join SIMEC scores, fill Ramsar gaps, and assign condition
  habitat_w_simec <- habitat_matched %>%
    left_join(i_efectividad_raw, by = c("nombre_matched" = "nombre")) %>%
    mutate(
      protected_area_condition = ifelse(!is.na(i_efectividad), i_efectividad, NA_real_)
    ) %>%
    # Fill in condition for protected areas with no SIMEC score (e.g. Ramsar sites
    # not managed by CONANP): join management plan status and assign score
    left_join(ramsar_management_plans, by = c("protected_area_name" = "wdpa_orig_name")) %>%
    mutate(
      protected_area_condition = case_when(
        !is.na(protected_area_condition)              ~ protected_area_condition, # SIMEC score takes priority
        if_ramsar_has_management_plan == "y"          ~ as.numeric(max(i_efectividad_raw$i_efectividad)),
        if_ramsar_has_management_plan == "in_progress" ~ 60,
        if_ramsar_has_management_plan == "n"          ~ as.numeric(min(i_efectividad_raw$i_efectividad)),
        TRUE                                          ~ NA_real_  # in protected area but no score available
      ),
      nom_condition  = nom_condition,
      # pmax: NOM score is a legal floor; ANP/Ramsar score only wins if stronger
      overall_condition = pmax(protected_area_condition, nom_condition, na.rm = TRUE),
      habitat_type      = habitat_label
    )

  # 5. One row per original feature (collapse multiple protected-area matches)
  habitat_condition <- habitat_w_simec %>%
    group_by(rgn_id, {{ name_col }}) %>%
    summarize(
      overall_condition        = mean(overall_condition, na.rm = TRUE),
      protected_area_condition = mean(protected_area_condition, na.rm = TRUE),
      in_protected_area        = any(in_protected_area),
      habitat_type             = first(habitat_type),
      geometry                 = st_union(geometry),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  

  return(habitat_condition)
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 2. Coquina Reefs
# ============================================================

coquina_reefs_condition <- assign_habitat_condition(
  coquina_reef_lsps,
  name_col = lsp_name,
  habitat_label  = "Coquina Reef",
  nom_condition  = NOM_COQUINA_CONDITION
)

rgn_coquina_reefs_condition <- coquina_reefs_condition %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(rgn_id) %>%
  summarize(
    condition  = mean(overall_condition, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_features = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mapview(coquina_reefs_condition, zcol = "overall_condition") + mapview(all_protected)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 3. Coral Reefs (Region 4 only: Cabo Pulmo / Los Frailes / Bahía San Gabriel)
# ============================================================

coral_reefs_condition <- assign_habitat_condition(
  coral_reefs_lsps,
  name_col = lsp_name,
  habitat_label = "Coral Reef",
  nom_condition = NOM_CORAL_CONDITION
)

rgn_coral_reefs_condition <- coral_reefs_condition %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(rgn_id) %>%
  summarize(
    condition  = mean(overall_condition, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_features = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mapview(coral_reefs_condition, zcol = "overall_condition") + mapview(all_protected)
```

```{r}

seagrass_condition <- assign_habitat_condition(

  nom_condition = NOM_SEAGRASS_CONDITION
)

rgn_seagrass_condition <- seagrass_condition %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(rgn_id) %>%
  summarize(
    condition  = mean(overall_condition, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_features = n(),

  )

mapview(seagrass_condition, zcol = "overall_condition") + mapview(all_protected)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 5. Mangroves
# ============================================================

mangroves_condition <- assign_habitat_condition(
  mangrove_lsps,
  name_col      = lsp_name,
  habitat_label = "Mangrove",
  nom_condition = NOM_MANGROVE_CONDITION
)

rgn_mangroves_condition <- mangroves_condition %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(rgn_id) %>%
  summarize(

mapview(mangroves_condition, zcol = "overall_condition") + mapview(all_protected)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 6. Combine all habitats and summarize by region
# ============================================================

rgn_all_habitats_condition <- bind_rows(
  rgn_coquina_reefs_condition,
  rgn_coral_reefs_condition,
  rgn_seagrass_condition,
  rgn_mangroves_condition
)

# per-region condition: mean across all habitat features in that region
rgn_special_habitats_condition <- rgn_all_habitats_condition %>%
  group_by(rgn_id) %>%
  summarize(
    condition  = mean(condition, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_features = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(rgn_special_habitats_condition)
```
